title: Paints & Coatings — DPP characteristics
description: Field specifications for the Paints & Coatings Digital Product Passport, shaped for UNTP's credentialSubject.characteristics extension point. Economic operators and facility identifiers are carried by the UNTP envelope and are deliberately absent here.

gtin.title: GTIN
gtin.description: Global Trade Item Number (GTIN-14) for the product.
gtin.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text.

ingredientSubstanceName.title: Substance Name
ingredientSubstanceName.description: Chemical name of the ingredient substance.

ingredientIupacName.title: IUPAC Name
ingredientIupacName.description: IUPAC systematic chemical name of the substance.
ingredientIupacName.x-citationNote: CLP governs how a substance is IDENTIFIED on the label and in classification, through the Art. 18(3) product identifier rules — a name, not an amount. It creates no duty to publish an IUPAC name as product data; the label and the safety data sheet are the channels through which composition information reaches users.

ingredientCasNumber.title: CAS Number
ingredientCasNumber.description: Chemical Abstracts Service registry number for the ingredient.

ingredientEcNumber.title: EC Number
ingredientEcNumber.description: European Community number (EINECS/ELINCS) for the substance.

ingredientReachRegistrationNumber.title: REACH Registration Number
ingredientReachRegistrationNumber.description: REACH registration number assigned by ECHA.
ingredientReachRegistrationNumber.x-citationNote: A REACH registration number is assigned to the registrant and appears in section 1 of the safety data sheet supplied down the chain under Art. 31. REACH creates no duty to publish it as product data, and for a mixture it is the constituent substances that carry registrations, not the product.

preservatives.title: Preservatives
preservatives.description: Array of preservatives with substance name and CAS number.
preservatives.x-citationNote: Preservatives reach consumers through the CLP label and, where applicable, sector labelling rules; CLP itself creates no separate duty to publish a preservative list as product data. Its labelling duty is discharged by what is affixed to the package.

fragranceAllergens.title: Fragrance Allergens
fragranceAllergens.description: Array of fragrance allergens present above threshold, with CAS numbers.
fragranceAllergens.x-citationNote: Fragrance allergen disclosure is a LABELLING duty in the sector instruments that impose it, not a CLP one — CLP's own obligation is the hazard label. Publishing the list here is useful to allergic users but is not how the duty is discharged.

hazardClass.title: Hazard Classes
hazardClass.description: Array of CLP/GHS hazard classifications applicable to the product.
hazardClass.x-citationNote: CLP Arts. 17-21 put the hazard information on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous. A labelling duty, not a passport one; empty for an unclassified mixture. No instrument creates a passport for paints.

signalWord.title: Signal Word
signalWord.x-citationNote: CLP Art. 20: the signal word ('Danger' or 'Warning') goes on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous; an unclassified mixture has none. A labelling duty, not a passport one. No instrument creates a passport for paints.

hazardPictograms.title: Hazard Pictograms
hazardPictograms.description: Array of GHS pictogram codes applicable to the product (GHS01 through GHS09).
hazardPictograms.x-citationNote: CLP Art. 19: hazard pictograms go on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous; none for an unclassified mixture. A labelling duty, not a passport one. No instrument creates a passport for paints.

hazardStatements.title: Hazard Statements
hazardStatements.description: Array of H-code hazard statements with full text.
hazardStatements.x-citationNote: CLP Art. 21: hazard statements (H-codes) go on the label of a mixture classified as hazardous; none for an unclassified mixture. A labelling duty, not a passport one. No instrument creates a passport for paints.

precautionaryStatements.title: Precautionary Statements
precautionaryStatements.description: Array of P-code precautionary statements with full text.

supplementalHazardInfo.title: Supplemental Hazard Information
supplementalHazardInfo.x-citationNote: CLP Annex II covers supplemental label information — EUH statements and similar. The obligation is to place that text ON THE LABEL; a passport copy repeats it rather than discharging it.

ufi.title: Unique Formula Identifier (UFI)
ufi.description: 16-character alphanumeric code linking the product to its poison centre notification. Required for hazardous mixtures.
ufi.x-citationNote: CLP Annex VIII Part A 3.1 and Art. 25(7): a UFI for mixtures classified for health or physical hazards and notified under Art. 45; not for mixtures classified only as gases under pressure or explosives (point 2.2). A labelling and notification duty, not a passport one. No instrument creates a passport for paints. Bespoke paints may opt out (Annex VIII 2.2a).

poisonCentreNotificationNumber.title: Poison Centre Notification Number
poisonCentreNotificationNumber.description: Notification number from ECHA poison centres notification portal.
poisonCentreNotificationNumber.x-citationNote: CLP Annex VIII governs notification of hazardous mixtures to the bodies appointed under Art. 45 for emergency health response. The duty is discharged by NOTIFYING those bodies — a database entry — and the resulting UFI belongs on the label. Publishing the notification reference in a passport neither creates nor satisfies the obligation.

emergencyPhoneNumber.title: Emergency Phone Number
emergencyPhoneNumber.description: 24-hour emergency telephone number for chemical incidents.

productCategoryEuPCS.title: EU Product Categorisation System (EuPCS)
productCategoryEuPCS.description: Product category code under the European Product Categorisation System for poison centre notifications.

svhcSubstances.title: SVHC / Substances of Concern
svhcSubstances.description: Array of Substances of Very High Concern present above 0.1% w/w. REACH Art. 33 applies to articles, not mixtures; for detergents and paints the relevant duty is the safety data sheet (Art. 31(1)(c), 31(3)(b)). For detergents, Annex VI Part A(h) of Reg (EU) 2026/405 covers SVHCs in the passport. The passport is not compelled to carry this by REACH Art. 33.
svhcSubstances.x-citationNote: REACH Art. 33 applies to articles, not mixtures. For a paint the SVHC duty is the safety data sheet (REACH Art. 31(1)(c), 31(3)(b)); no instrument requires a passport to carry this list.

svhcEcNumber.title: SVHC EC Number
svhcEcNumber.description: EC number for the SVHC substance.
svhcEcNumber.x-citationNote: REACH Art. 33 is the SVHC communication duty and it is narrower than it looks: to business recipients, and to consumers ON REQUEST within 45 days, for articles containing an SVHC above 0.1% w/w, with a minimum content of the substance NAME. Publishing an EC number proactively exceeds what any in-force provision requires.

svhcLocationInProduct.title: SVHC Location in Product
svhcLocationInProduct.description: Where in the product the SVHC substance is present.
svhcLocationInProduct.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. svhcCandidateListDate.title: SVHC Candidate List Date
svhcCandidateListDate.description: Date when the substance was added to the ECHA SVHC candidate list.
svhcCandidateListDate.x-citationNote: REACH Art. 59 governs how a substance is added to the candidate list. The date of inclusion determines when the Art. 33 communication and SCIP notification duties bite for that substance; it is a fact about the list rather than a datum the manufacturer is required to publish.

svhcScipNotificationId.title: SCIP Notification ID
svhcScipNotificationId.description: SCIP database notification identifier from ECHA for articles containing SVHCs.
svhcScipNotificationId.x-citationNote: The SCIP database notification is required by Waste Framework Directive Art. 9(1)(i), in force since 5 January 2021, for articles containing candidate-list substances above 0.1% w/w. The duty is discharged by notifying ECHA — a database entry — not by publishing the resulting identifier.

vocContent.title: VOC Content
vocContent.description: Volatile Organic Compound content of the paint or varnish as formulated. The ready-to-use limit is in vocContentReadyToUse (Decopaint Directive Art. 4(b)); this field records the measured value.
vocContent.x-citationNote: Directive 2004/42/EC Art. 4 requires the LABEL to indicate the maximum VOC content in g/l in a ready-to-use condition. The duty is discharged by that label; the Directive creates no passport and no separate publication duty.

vocLimit.title: VOC Limit
vocLimit.description: Maximum VOC limit for this product subcategory under the Decopaint Directive.
vocLimit.x-citationNote: Art. 4(a) requires the LABEL to indicate the relevant VOC limit values from Annex II alongside the subcategory. The limit itself is set by Annex II; Art. 3 makes staying under it a condition of placing the product on the market. The Annex II limit value for the product's subcategory, which Art. 4(a) requires on the LABEL. Art. 3 permits placing on the market only where the VOC content does not exceed it — a market-placement condition backed by a labelling duty.

vocCategory.title: VOC Category
vocCategory.description: Decopaint Directive product subcategory for VOC limits.
vocCategory.x-citationNote: It defines the product categories and subcategories in scope, and Art. 4(a) requires the subcategory to appear on the LABEL. It is a scoping and labelling construct rather than passport data.

paintType.title: Paint Type
paintType.description: Classification of the paint/coating product type.
paintType.x-citationNote: The Directive's operative distinction is the Annex I subcategory, which Art. 4(a) puts on the label. A free product-type description is not a mandated datum.

vocContentReadyToUse.title: VOC Content (Ready to Use)
vocContentReadyToUse.description: VOC content of the product when ready for use (after any prescribed dilution).
vocContentReadyToUse.x-citationNote: This is the exact datum Art. 4(b) requires on the LABEL — the maximum VOC content in g/l of the product in a ready-to-use condition. Real mandated data, discharged by affixing the label rather than by publishing here.

solventType.title: Solvent Type
solventType.description: Whether the product is water-borne or solvent-borne.
solventType.x-citationNote: Annex I distinguishes water-borne from solvent-borne products because they carry different Annex II limit values, so the distinction has legal effect — but what Art. 4 requires on the label is the subcategory and the VOC figures, not the solvent type itself.

coverageSqmPerLitre.title: Coverage (m²/L)
coverageSqmPerLitre.description: Spreading rate / coverage area per litre of product.

wetScrubResistanceClass.title: Wet Scrub Resistance Class
wetScrubResistanceClass.description: Wet scrub resistance class per EN 13300 (Class 1-5).

titaniumDioxideContent.title: Titanium Dioxide Content (%)
titaniumDioxideContent.description: Weight percentage of titanium dioxide (TiO2) in the product. Subject to CLP classification.
titaniumDioxideContent.x-citationNote: Titanium dioxide carries CLP classification and labelling consequences in certain forms, and any applicable hazard statement belongs on the LABEL. CLP creates no duty to publish a content figure as product data.

isoClassification.title: ISO Classification
isoClassification.description: ISO classification for paints and coatings (e.g. ISO 12944 for corrosion protection).
isoClassification.x-standard: ISO 12944 (corrosivity categories for protective paint systems)
